bonuses.name: Silver Owls
bonuses.description: Workers +10% metal gather rate per phase advance.
bonuses.history: The mines at Laureion in Attica provided Athens with a wealth of silver from which to mint her famous and highly prized coin, The Athenian Owl.

bonuses.name: Epilektoi Infantry
bonuses.description: Elite Hoplites can promote to Champion Spearmen.
bonuses.history: The best of the hoplites were chosen to form a group of elite professional soldiers.

bonuses.name: Spartan Women
bonuses.description: Female Citizens +40% health and +50% melee attack hack damage.

bonuses.name: Laws of Lycurgus
bonuses.description: Champion Hoplites are available in village phase, and can promote to highly experienced Olympic Champions.
bonuses.history: Under the constitution written by the mythical lawgiver Lycurgus, the institution of the Agoge was established, where Spartans were trained from the age of 6 to be superior warriors in defense of the Spartan state.

bonuses.name: Darics
bonuses.description: Land Traders +25% trade gain.

bonuses.name: Large Rams
bonuses.description: Battering Rams +20% attack damage and +2 garrison capacity.

bonuses.name: Times of War
bonuses.description: The batch training time of units trained in Stables decreases each phase advance.
bonuses.history: The Persians were known for their large cavalry contingent.

bonuses.name: Satrapy Tribute
bonuses.description: Upgrade the Throne Hall to receive a free trickle of a desired resource.
bonuses.history: The empire was divided into provinces, called “Satrapies,” that sent yearly tribute to the ruling Persian dynasty in Persepolis as a form of tax.

bonuses.name: Fertility
bonuses.description: Women train from houses without the need to research Fertility Festival.
bonuses.history: Rome was one of the most populous cities in the ancient world.

bonuses.name: Testudo Formation
bonuses.description: Roman Legionaries can form a Testudo.
bonuses.history: The Romans commonly used the Testudo or 'turtle' formation for defense: Legionaries were formed into hollow squares with twelve men on each side, standing so close together that their shields overlapped like fish scales.

bonuses.name: Centurions
bonuses.description: Promote Elite Rank Spearmen or Swordsmen to Champion Centurions.
bonuses.history: Centurions were the officers responsible for a centuria, a group of 100 soldiers.

bonuses.name: Commercial Acumen
bonuses.description: Merchant Ships +25% trade gain.

bonuses.name: Desirable Products
bonuses.description: Docks and Markets +10% international trade bonus.

bonuses.name: Deas Celtica
bonuses.description: Druids increase attack rates of soldiers near them by 5%.
bonuses.history: Celtic religion and druidry inspired their warlike mindset.

bonuses.name: Woad Warriors
bonuses.description: All Infantry Units +5% movement speed, and gain +1 loot taking.
bonuses.history: Britons paint their bodies with Woad, which produces a blue color and gives them a fiercesome appearance in battle.

bonuses.name: Deas Celtica
bonuses.description: Druids increase attack rates of soldiers near them by 5%.
bonuses.history: Celtic religion and druidry inspired their warlike mindset.

bonuses.name: Starting Walls
bonuses.description: Iberians start with City Walls around their base on most maps.
bonuses.history: With exception to alluvial plains and river valleys, stone is abundant in the Iberian Peninsula and was greatly used in construction of structures of all types.

bonuses.name: Massive Towers
bonuses.description: Stone Towers −50% wood cost, +150% stone cost, +33% build time, +60% health, +3 garrison capacity, and +1 default arrow count.

bonuses.name: Large Rams
bonuses.description: Battering Rams +20% attack damage and +2 garrison capacity.

bonuses.name: Polybolos
bonuses.description: Bolt Shooters −33% attack damage and −33% attack time.

bonuses.name: Nile Delta
bonuses.description: The three farming technologies are available in Village Phase.
bonuses.history: The Nile Delta is a region where the Nile River divides into several branches to flow into the Mediterranean Sea, in northern Egypt.

bonuses.name: Seeresses
bonuses.description: A unique Champion Healer unit is available in City Phase.
bonuses.history: Seeresses accompanied the Germanic armies and envisioned prophecies of victory from sacrifices.
